title: Federal definition of readily retrievable
rule_summary: Readily retrievable means that certain records are kept by automatic data processing systems or other electronic or mechanized recordkeeping systems in such a manner that they can be separated out from all other records in a reasonable time, and/or records are kept on which certain items are asterisked, redlined, or in some other manner visually identifiable apart from other items appearing on the records.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate applies the defined term as a test of separation in a reasonable time rather than as a requirement of physical segregation.
common_confusions: The definition is about the capability of the recordkeeping system, not about where the records physically sit.
verification_notes: Read in the current eCFR text of 21 CFR 1300.01(b) on ecfr.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
